title: `upper`, `lower`: full Unicode mappings (ICU by default, the JVM's under a conf), in the JVM's default locale
verdict: `char_set: UTF8` with full mappings (`ß` → `SS`, final sigma) under a JVM locale without special casing; ASCII fast path
description: `upper` and `lower` map ASCII text byte by byte and anything else with Java's `String.toUpperCase()` and `toLowerCase()`: Unicode's full mappings, context included. `upper('ß')` is `SS`, `upper('ﬁ')` `FI`, `upper('straße')` `STRASSE` (the length grows from 6 to 7), `lower('İ')` `i̇` (two code points), `lower('ΣΑΣ')` `σας` with a final sigma, `upper('ǅ')` `Ǆ`, `lower('Ⅻ')` `ⅻ`.

The no-argument `toUpperCase()` uses the JVM's default locale, so a JVM started in a Turkish or Azeri locale maps `i` to `İ` (a setting outside Spark's own configuration). The probes ran in an English locale.
reference: `upper`, `lower` with `char_set: UTF8`, a black box (Rust's `str::to_uppercase`, Unicode's full mappings); Lean evaluates them on ASCII only. ST-10 records that Substrait leaves simple and full mappings open. Spark's mappings are Unicode's full ones, as Rust's are, under a locale without special casing.

provenance.checked_by: the same probe under `uv run --with pyspark==<version>` (D51 facts, C3), one JVM per version, default settings

evidence.note: pyspark 4.0.1 and 4.1.1 map 1552 scalars for `upper` and 1460 for `lower`: 28 fewer in each direction than 4.3.0, newer additions (U+16EA0 to U+16EBF, U+A7CE to U+A7D5) that DuckDB does not map either: every one of them is in the raise sets already; pyspark 4.2.0 gives 4.3.0's table exactly. The table of the raise sets therefore holds for pyspark 4.0 to 4.3

provenance.checked_by: D51 facts (C2 of the ruling on the raise sets)

evidence.note: `spark.sql.icu.caseMappings.enabled` (since 4.0.0, default true): ICU, not the JVM, implements case mappings under UTF8_BINARY collation
`Upper.exec` and `Lower.exec`: `execBinaryICU` when the conf is on, `execBinary` (`UTF8String.toUpperCase`) when off
the default path: a fully ASCII string byte by byte, any other through ICU's `UCharacter.toUpperCase(String)` / `toLowerCase(String)`, which take the default locale
the JVM path: `String.toUpperCase()` / `toLowerCase()` without a locale argument, so the JVM's default locale

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.case_tables --spark-setting (D51 facts, pyspark 4.3.0, OpenJDK 21.0.13, ICU 78.3 with Unicode 17)

evidence.note: every scalar under the ICU path (the default) and the JVM path (`spark.sql.icu.caseMappings.enabled=false`), in the JVM's default locale (de_DE here) and with `user.language` tr, az and lt, as differences from the default table. The JVM path lacks 55 pairs ICU has (`upper('ƛ')`, U+019B to U+A7DC): scalars DuckDB leaves alone too, so they are in the raise sets already. tr and az: `lower('İ')` is `i`, and in a string with a non-ASCII scalar `I` lowers to `ı` and `i` uppercases to `İ` (`lower('Ié')` is `ıé`); lt: `lower` of `Ì`, `Í`, `Ĩ` keeps a dot above

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.case_tables (D51 facts, pyspark 4.3.0 on OpenJDK 21, macOS arm64)

evidence.note: every Unicode scalar value (without surrogates) through `upper` and `lower` alone: 1580 values for `upper` and 1488 for `lower`, the same as Polars; full mappings, and a final sigma; the context strings of `CONTEXT` are in the file's `context`

the values the three tier-1 engines map differently: 157 for `upper`, 56 for `lower` (213 in all, none in both); Polars and Spark agree on every one-character string, so each is DuckDB's simple mapping against their full one, and the final sigma is a context rule apart from them

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `lower` of the UTF8_BINARY column turns `İo` into `i̇o`: `i` plus U+0307, two code points for one
`upper` of the same rows: `İo` → `İO`, ASCII rows upper-cased byte by byte

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.
